relations.subject: server:rebalance
relations.evidence: Gets rebalance status information for the cluster. Currently the status either reports "running" or "not running".

notable_absence.finding: This command exposes only a binary 'running' or 'not running' status - literally stated: 'Currently the status either reports "running" or "not running".' No percentage-complete, ETA, or per-service/per-bucket breakdown is exposed, despite the rebalance subcommand's own --no-progress-bar / --no-wait flags implying a richer progress-tracking concept exists elsewhere (e.g. the Web Console's progress bar). This CLI status command doesn't surface that granularity at all - a real capability/documentation gap between what the CLI can report and what the product visibly tracks.

cross_component_finding: This page's DESCRIPTION is a single terse sentence and its OPTIONS/HOST FORMATS/CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION/ENVIRONMENT AND CONFIGURATION VARIABLES sections are the exact same universal boilerplate already documented across essentially every other couchbase-cli page in this and prior batches (word-for-word, down to the six base flags). No content on this page is specific to rebalance-status beyond its one-sentence DESCRIPTION, its single EXAMPLES command, and its SEE ALSO list - consistent with terse, lightly-reviewed engineer-authored reference prose. No cbcli-vs-REST/UI terminology drift is visible on this page specifically, since it introduces almost no unique vocabulary of its own to drift.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella, where rebalance is managed automatically and this kind of manual status polling has no customer-facing equivalent.
